newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-PENAROL'S DREAM SHATTERED IN SHOOT-OUT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PENAROL'S DREAM SHATTERED IN SHOOT-OUT.

text.p: Penarol's dream of a return to greatness was shattered when they were beaten on penalties by Argentina's Racing Club in their Libertadores Cup quarter-final on Wednesday.

Sporting Cristal became the first Peruvian side to reach the semifinals for 20 years by knocking out Bolivar while Colo Colo emerged victorious from the duel between the two Chilean quarter-finalists.

Uruguay's Penarol, five times Libertadores champions, were once one of the world's great clubs. In their heyday, they were an equal match for Europe's finest teams, winning the world club title on three occasions.
But, in a decline which is symbolic of the flagging fortunes of their country's soccer, they had failed to progress beyond the second round of the competition since their last triumph 10 years ago.
Penarol took a 1-0 lead to Buenos Aires but their advantage was wiped out within four minutes by Ruben Capria.

The Uruguayans had the better of the rest of the first half but the game petered out after the interval. Gonzalo de los Santos of Penarol and Mauro Navas of Racing were sent off for fighting early in the second half.

Argentina goalkeeper Ignacio Gonzalez, currently serving a three-match World Cup ban for head-butting a Bolivian opponent, was the hero as Racing won the shootout 3-2. Gonzalez converted a penalty for his own team and saved two Penarol efforts while another Uruguayan penalty flew wide.
Bolivar, who led 2-1 from a first leg played at 3,700 metres altitude, suffered at sea level as they lost 3-0 to Sporting Cristal in Lima.

Veteran Cameroon goalkeeper Thomas N'Kono kept the Bolivians level for half an hour with some fine saves but goals by Nolberto Solano, Jorge Soto and Ghana's Prince Amoako gave Cristal a comfortable 4-2 aggregate win.
Bolivar had Ivan Castillo sent off in the second half as the game turned rough.
Colo Colo, trailing 2-1 from the first leg against local rivals Universidad Catolica, also overturned their disadvantage by winning 3-1 in Santiago.
Colo Colo, the only Chilean team to have won the title, meet the winners of the all-Brazilian tie between Gremio and Cruzeiro in the semifinals.
